negation_types.description: Negates value type constraints (NOT IRI, NOT LITERAL)
negation_types.use_case: Exclude specific value types from a property
negation_types.example: ex:name !IRI  // name must NOT be an IRI

negation_types.use_case: Prohibit specific values while allowing others
negation_types.example: ex:status ![ex:deleted ex:archived]  // status cannot be deleted or archived

negation_types.use_case: Assert that a property must NOT satisfy certain constraints
negation_types.example: !(ex:email LITERAL)  // if ex:email exists, it must NOT be a literal

negation_types.description: Negates shape reference (ShapeNot in W3C spec)
negation_types.use_case: Assert node does NOT conform to a shape
negation_types.example: ex:person !@PersonShape  // person value must NOT conform to PersonShape

negation_types.use_case: Complex validation rules using De Morgan's laws
negation_types.example: !(ex:type IRI OR ex:type BNODE)  // type is neither IRI nor BNODE (must be LITERAL)

algorithm: 1. If negation == NOT, validate normally then invert result
2. Check excludedValueType: if type matches excluded type, return false
3. Check excludedIris: if value in excluded set, return false
ValueSetConstraint_validate.complexity: O(1) for type checks, O(log n) for IRI set lookups with hash set

algorithm: 1. For AND: all operands must validate (short-circuit on first false)
2. For OR: at least one operand must validate (short-circuit on first true)
3. For each operand: apply its negation before combining results
LogicalExpression_validate.complexity: O(k) where k is number of operands, with short-circuit optimization

algorithm: 1. Check negatedShapeRefs: validate against each shape, ensure ALL fail
2. For properties with negation: validate and invert result
4. Apply De Morgan optimizations where applicable
Shape_validateNegation.complexity: O(n*m) where n is number of properties, m is number of negated shapes

rules: NOT (A AND B) => (NOT A) OR (NOT B)
NOT (A OR B) => (NOT A) AND (NOT B)
NOT (A AND NOT B) => (NOT A) OR B

validation_overhead.simple_negation: Negligible - adds one boolean inversion O(1)

validation_overhead.logical_composition: O(k) where k is number of sub-expressions, reduced by short-circuiting
validation_overhead.shape_negation: O(V_ref) where V_ref is cost of validating referenced shape - can be expensive
validation_overhead.nested_negations: Depth d adds multiplicative factor, but De Morgan optimization reduces depth

optimization_strategies.benefit: Simplifies nested negations, reduces validation depth
optimization_strategies.implementation: Apply during parsing or lazy application during validation
optimization_strategies.example: !(A AND B) -> (!A OR !B) enables short-circuit OR instead of full AND evaluation

optimization_strategies.benefit: Stops validation early when result determined
optimization_strategies.implementation: For AND: return false on first failure; for OR: return true on first success
optimization_strategies.savings: Up to 50-90% reduction in validation steps for large logical expressions

optimization_strategies.benefit: Cache results of negated shape validations
optimization_strategies.implementation: Add validation cache: map<(nodeId, shapeId), result>
optimization_strategies.tradeoff: Memory for speed - useful for repeated validations on same dataset

optimization_strategies.implementation: Simplify (A OR !A) -> true, (A AND !A) -> false during parsing
optimization_strategies.savings: Eliminates runtime validation for trivially true/false constraints

optimization_strategies.benefit: Don't build full expression tree until needed
optimization_strategies.implementation: Use std::function or lazy evaluation wrappers
optimization_strategies.tradeoff: Complexity vs. memory - best for rarely-used complex constraints

deeply_nested_negations.mitigation: Double negation elimination during parsing: !!A -> A

negated_expensive_shapes.impact: Must fully validate ComplexShape to invert result
negated_expensive_shapes.mitigation: Early termination: if ComplexShape validation can determine conformance early, stop

large_exclusion_sets.mitigation: Use absl::flat_hash_set for O(1) average case lookups

test_cases.name: Test 3: Logical Composition with De Morgan Optimization
test_cases.description: Value must be LITERAL (neither IRI nor BNODE)
test_cases.demorgan_transformation: !(IRI OR BNODE) => (!IRI AND !BNODE) => must be LITERAL
test_cases.validation_logic: Parse as LogicalExpression{NOT, {OR, [IRI, BNODE]}} => optimize to LogicalExpression{AND, [NOT IRI, NOT BNODE]}
test_cases.optimization_benefit: AND with short-circuit: fails fast on first non-matching type

test_cases.name: Test 4: Negated Shape Reference
test_cases.description: Author must NOT be a bot (must not conform to BotShape)

test_data.reason: user1 data does not conform to BotShape (missing automated/version)
bot1 data conforms to BotShape, violating !@BotShape constraint
semi-auto partially matches BotShape but missing version, so doesn't fully conform

test_cases.validation_logic: Validate author against BotShape, expect validation to FAIL for DocumentShape to be valid
test_cases.complexity_note: Requires recursive shape validation - most expensive negation type

test_cases.name: Test 5: Complex Nested Negation with Multiple De Morgan Applications
test_cases.description: Complex filter logic with nested negations
demorgan_transformation: Step 2: !(IRI AND !LITERAL) AND !(BNODE AND !IRI)  [De Morgan on OR]
Step 3: (!IRI OR !!LITERAL) AND (!BNODE OR !!IRI)  [De Morgan on each AND]
Step 4: (!IRI OR LITERAL) AND (!BNODE OR IRI)      [Double negation elimination]
Final: (LITERAL if not IRI) AND (IRI if not BNODE)

test_data.reason: LITERAL satisfies (!IRI OR LITERAL)=true AND (!BNODE OR IRI)=true
IRI satisfies (!IRI OR LITERAL)=LITERAL AND (!BNODE OR IRI)=true
BNODE: (!IRI OR LITERAL)=true AND (!BNODE OR IRI)=false => overall false

test_cases.validation_logic: Multi-step De Morgan transformation simplifies complex negation to evaluable form
test_cases.optimization_showcase: Without De Morgan: deeply nested validation; With De Morgan: flat OR/AND chains with short-circuit
